summary.text: 手 is a pictograph of a hand. Bronze forms are interpreted as showing fingers above a lower part described as an arm or palm; the exact anatomy is unsettled. The earliest graph evidence identified here comes from Western Zhou bronze materials, though those examples do not establish a dated use meaning “hand.”

formation.text: Pictographic (象形): 手 depicts a hand as a whole. Paleographic interpretations identify branching strokes as fingers and the lower part as an arm or palm. No separate sound component or internal component split is supported.

history.text: The curated bronze-style image represents a form catalogued among Western Zhou materials; the seal-style image represents a seal-script form. Both are modern redrawings, not artifact photographs, and they do not by themselves establish a direct sequence of graphic change.
Paleographic discussions report 手 absent from oracle-bone inscriptions and distinguish other hand-shaped graphs. The cited material does not identify an oracle-bone form of 手.

uncertainties.text: Accounts differ on whether the lower part of the bronze graph represents an arm alone or includes the palm. Its exact anatomy remains an interpretation.

Bronze examples are catalogued from the Western Zhou onward, but no individual earliest inscription date or semantic context for those occurrences is established. The early hand meaning is supported by graphic interpretation and later lexicographic analysis.
The spoken-word history of 手 and proposed comparisons with Proto-Sino-Tibetan vocabulary, Burmese, and 收 are not established by the cited material.

senses.period: Western Zhou bronze materials (earliest graph evidence identified; semantic context unverified)
senses.text: The graph is interpreted as depicting a hand, and later lexicographic evidence supports this meaning. The bronze occurrences themselves lack verified semantic contexts, so they do not establish a securely dated earliest use with this meaning.
Shuowen glosses 手 as 拳 (“fist”). Its commentator explains hand and fist as mutually explanatory; this account does not establish that “fist” was the original meaning.
A historical dictionary records this use with a citation to 宋書, but the evidence here does not establish when it arose or how it developed from the hand sense.
A historical dictionary records this use with a citation to 漢書, without establishing its date or a semantic pathway from the bodily sense.
A historical dictionary records 手 as a verb meaning “hold,” with a citation to 公羊傳. Its chronological relation to the hand noun is not established here.

limitations.text: The bronze graph evidence gives no semantic contexts, and the transmitted classical citations are not independently dated excavated attestations. The evidence does not establish chronological priority among these uses or transitions connecting them.

overview.text: 手 depicts a hand as a whole. Early bronze forms are interpreted as showing finger branches above an arm or palm, though the precise anatomy is unsettled.
